newsitem.title: USA: FBI alerts Getty, socialite about Cunanan - report.
newsitem.headline: FBI alerts Getty, socialite about Cunanan - report.

text.p: The FBI has alerted oil heir Gordon Getty and a San Francisco socialite they could be among the next targets of suspected spree killer Andrew Cunanan, the San Francisco Chronicle reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said Getty and socialite Harry de Wildt, both prominent San Franciscans, had been warned by the FBI about Cunanan, who is suspected of gunning down fashion designer Gianni Versace outside his Miami Beach mansion last week.
Cunanan, 27, also wanted in four other murders, has spent time in San Francisco in the past.
The newspaper quoted De Wildt as saying that the FBI had contacted him last week. "It seems that Gordon Getty and I were two people who they felt should be warned," de Wildt was quoted as saying.
According to de Wildt, the report said, both his name and Getty's popped up in FBI interviews with people whom Cunanan knew from his past stays in San Francisco.
Gordon Getty is a son of late billionaire oil tycoon J. Paul Getty.

"It seems that Gordon and I are two of his biggest idols here in San Francisco. Apparently he admired our (high society) lifestyles, much like he admired Gianni Versace for his success," in the fashion world," the Chronicle quoted de Wildt as saying.

The Chronicle said a Getty family spokeswoman declined to comment. The FBI would not confirm talking to either Getty or de Wildt but did acknowledge contacting a number of celebrity figures whom Cunanan claimed to know, the paper said.
Getty and de Wildt could not be reached for comment on Wednesday.
George Grotz, an FBI spokesman in San Francisco, said the FBI had "identified various individuals and we have talked to them" about Cunanan. "That is a prudent thing for us to do," he said.
"Some of them may possibly come to his attention or be a target," Grotz said.
But he declined to say whether the FBI had spoken to Getty or de Wildt, saying it was the FBI's longstanding policy not to reveal who it had talked to.
